2027-01-22.title: Friday after the Second Sunday after Denho · Mar Timotheos the Apostle
readings: Fight the good fight of the faith
Not to abolish but to fulfil
2027-01-22.alt: Season of Denho. Commemoration of Mar Timotheos, disciple of St Paul. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-22.verse: Fight the good fight of the faith; take hold of the eternal life, to which you were called and for which you made the good confession in the presence of many witnesses.
theo: Today our Church remembers Mar Timotheos, the young disciple whom Paul called “my loyal child in the faith”. Paul's charge to him is a programme for every Christian: “pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, gentleness. Fight the good fight of the faith; take hold of the eternal life, to which you were called.” Timothy was timid, often unwell and young for his office, yet he became a shepherd of the church in Ephesus. God's strength is shown in such weakness.

In the Gospel Jesus says: “Do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets; I have come not to abolish but to fulfill.” The Christian faith does not throw away the Old Testament; it reads it in the light of Christ, as our liturgy does every day. Timothy learned the Scriptures from childhood at the knees of his mother and grandmother, and Paul taught him to see Christ in them. Our families too can be the first school of the word.
outline: Ask: who first taught you the faith?
Christ completes the law and prophets.
“Fight the good fight of the faith.”
live: Choose one of the six virtues Paul lists and practise it today.

2027-01-22.prayer: Lord Jesus, you came not to abolish but to fulfil. Through the prayers of Mar Timotheos make us fight the good fight of the faith, take hold of eternal life, and hand on the faith in our homes as Lois and Eunice did. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono the Old Testament and the Gospel are read together: Christ fulfils all, and then gives himself to us.

quick: Fight the good fight of the faith.

2027-01-22.question: Am I fighting the good fight, or have I given up?

family.explain: Timothy learned about God from his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice. Our families teach us about God too!
family.intention: We pray in thanksgiving for those who taught us the faith.
family.ask: Ask: “Who taught you your first prayer?”

illus: A priest from Marthandam remembers that his grandmother could not read, but she knew the Psalms by heart from years of the Church's prayers. Each evening she sang them as she lit the lamp. He says: I learned the Scriptures from her mouth before I learned them from a book, just as Timothy did.

pm.open: Lord, make us faithful disciples like Timothy, fighting the good fight of the faith. Amen.
share: Pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, gentleness (1 Timothy 6:11). Which do I most need?
I have come not to abolish but to fulfill (Matthew 5:17). Do I read the Old Testament with Christ in view?
A faith that lived first in your grandmother (2 Timothy 1:5). Whose faith lives in me?
interc: For bishops and priests, through Mar Timotheos.
For young people called to ministry.
For parents and grandparents who teach the faith.
pm.close: Father, you gave Timothy as a shepherd to your Church. Make us faithful in the good fight and generous in handing on the faith. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today we remember Mar Timotheos, the young disciple of St Paul. Paul charges him: pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, gentleness. Fight the good fight of the faith; take hold of the eternal life, to which you were called (1 Timothy 6:11–12).
Timothy was young, timid and often sick, yet he became a shepherd of the church in Ephesus. God's strength works through our weakness.

In the Gospel Jesus says: I have come not to abolish but to fulfill (Matthew 5:17). The Old Testament is not thrown away; Christ fulfils it. Timothy learned the Scriptures from his mother and grandmother.
Let our homes too be schools of the word. Let us fight the good fight and hand on the faith. Amen.
kids: Children, Timothy learned about God from his mother and grandmother. Who teaches you about God? Thank them today!

Mar Timotheos: the good fight, Christ's fulfilment, and faith handed on at home.

sub: Reading the Old Testament in his light.
q: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the LORD: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
“Do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets; I have come not to abolish but to fulfill.
points.apply: Read one Old Testament reading this week and ask how it points to Christ.

q: Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.
I am reminded of your sincere faith, a faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and now, I am sure, lives in you.

concl: Timothy fought the good fight in weakness.
